scope: Primary-source refresh for German-first local realtime voice. Source evidence only; no target-runtime, German E2E, Trigger4, or acceptance credit.

observed: FastTurn combines acoustic cues with streaming CTC-derived semantic cues for low-latency turn detection.
Its released test set explicitly includes overlap, backchannels, pauses, pitch variation and environmental noise.
findings.project_delta: Promote FastTurn from generic literature reference to a high-value T7-TURN-001 discriminator/dataset-method donor. It is especially relevant to Frankenstein's false-endpoint, overlap, backchannel and interruption tests.
findings.negative_space: No German-specific endpoint quality, target-host latency, cancellation correctness, or Frankenstein ABI integration was observed here. Do not promote to V3/V4/V5 from paper/repo evidence.

observed: Official Qwen3-TTS exposes 0.6B/1.7B models, Apache-2.0 source, German support, streaming speech generation, voice design and voice cloning.
Current package metadata pins transformers 4.57.3 and includes accelerate, torchaudio, onnxruntime and other runtime dependencies.

Open issue traffic includes streaming-mode/runtime and FlashAttention/compatibility problems, so advertised streaming capability is not equivalent to reproducible Frankenstein target-runtime behavior.
findings.project_delta: Keep Qwen3-TTS first in the expressive German TTS benchmark order, but explicitly gate its streaming claim on target-host TTFA/RTF/cancellation reproduction. Piper/Thorsten remains the tiny deterministic latency floor rather than the quality winner by assumption.
findings.negative_space: No local Frankenstein target-host execution, male-voice identity stability, ExpressionVector control, German pronunciation score, TTFA, RTF or long-session evidence was observed in this run.

observed: German Thorsten Piper ONNX artifacts remain available under MIT metadata.
The high model is approximately 114 MB and exposes a published SHA-256 on Hugging Face.
findings.project_delta: Retain Piper/Thorsten as the low-footprint deterministic German TTS latency/resource floor for the same host and sentence corpus used by expressive challengers.
findings.negative_space: No claim that Piper matches the desired conversational naturalness or state-driven expressive control.

observed: Qwen3-ASR-0.6B remains an Apache-2.0 multilingual ASR candidate with explicit German support.
The current Hugging Face model tree reports a roughly 1.88 GB safetensors model artifact.
findings.project_delta: No ranking promotion beyond existing T7-ASR-001. The decisive test remains identical real German room audio against donor Whisper and Nemotron 3.5 Streaming under measured endpoint/partial-transcript latency.
findings.negative_space: No target-host WER/CER/latency evidence in this run.

observed: Official Qwen3.5-4B remains available under Apache-2.0 with local Transformers/vLLM/SGLang serving guidance.

The current unquantized safetensors repository is materially larger than the desired resident Q4 voice-brain deployment, reinforcing the need for an immutable quantized reference before comparing the abliterated Q4.
findings.project_delta: Preserve checkpoint order: official Qwen3.5-4B quantized reference first, then abliterated controlled variant under identical German VoiceSessionCapsule prompts.
findings.negative_space: No immutable official Q4 artifact was pinned by this source-only refresh and no VPS model load occurred.

hypothesis_update: Lane A remains favored. The strongest near-term improvement is not another model swap but tighter causal turn control: streaming ASR plus acoustic-semantic endpoint intelligence feeding cancellation-safe local inference and expressive streaming TTS.
counterhypothesis: FastTurn-like semantic endpointing may add model/ASR latency and complexity without improving German Frankenstein turn behavior enough to beat a tuned acoustic VAD plus simpler endpoint heuristic.
cheapest_high_information_discriminator: On clay-direct-dev, replay a pinned German pause/backchannel/overlap corpus through donor VAD/endpoint logic versus a FastTurn-derived or equivalent acoustic-semantic controller while holding ASR/audio transport fixed; compare false endpoints, late endpoints and barge-in cancellation latency.
